items.title: Épanouissement familial : CAFAS-TOURLET lance officiellement ses activités à Ouagadougou
items.description: Le Cercle d'accompagnement familial et social Tourlet (CAFAS-TOURLET) a officiellement lancé ses activités, le samedi 14 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou. Ce cabinet, spécialisé dans l'accompagnement et le développement familial et social, entend soutenir les parents dans l'éducation de leurs enfants, sans jamais se substituer aux familles. Placée sous le patronage d'Ourobé Éric Coulibaly, Secrétaire général du ministère de la Famille et de la Solidarité, et sous le marrainage de Karidia Sinka/Dramé, Psychologue consultante, la cérémonie de lancement a été marquée par la coupure officielle du ruban. Dans une société en pleine mutation, où les enfants sont rapidement confrontés à d'autres modes de vie, assurer leur éducation au sein de la famille constitue un défi pour de nombreux parents. La famille constitue pourtant le premier cadre d'éducation, de protection et de développement de l'individu. C'est pour relever ce défi que le Cercle d'accompagnement familial et social Tourlet (CAFAS-TOURLET) propose un accompagnement spécialisé, humain et adapté aux réalités du Burkina Faso. Selon son directeur général, Lucien Kéré, Tourlet, qui signifie « éducation » en bissa, a pour mission principale de conseiller et d'accompagner les familles sans se substituer à elles. Il s'agit notamment de renforcer les liens familiaux, de soutenir le développement humain et de contribuer à la construction de familles plus unies et résilientes. « Nous avons plusieurs domaines d'intervention. En matière de famille et de couple, le cabinet se propose de préparer la jeunesse au mariage. Nous conseillons les couples. Il y a aussi la médiation familiale, la gestion des conflits et la prévention des violences conjugales, qui sont des problématiques sociales que nous travaillons à résoudre chez les couples », a-t-il déclaré. Lucien Kéré, DG, de CAFAS-TOURLTET, a présenté les missions de cette initiative sociale CAFAS-TOURLET prévoit également un accompagnement psychologique destiné aux couples et aux familles confrontés à des difficultés relationnelles. Le secrétaire général du ministère de la Famille et de la Solidarité, Ourobé Éric Coulibaly, en sa qualité de patron de la cérémonie, a salué une initiative nouvelle qui vient renforcer les mécanismes de protection et de bien-être des familles, à travers la préparation au mariage et à la vie de couple, le suivi scolaire et éducatif des enfants, les camps et clubs de vacances ainsi que l'accompagnement des personnes âgées. Ourobé Éric Coulibaly, SG MFS, patron de l'événement a invité les initiateurs à être proche des familles Aussi a-t-il invité les responsables du centre à respecter la réglementation, à garantir la confidentialité des bénéficiaires, à placer leur intérêt au cœur des prestations, à rendre les services accessibles aux familles modestes et à travailler en complémentarité avec les structures publiques. « Vous n'êtes pas venus remplacer les structures de l'État, vous êtes venus jouer votre rôle en tant qu'acteur privé, en complémentarité avec l'existence des structures gouvernementales. Il faudrait étudier vos tarifs pour que les familles les plus modestes aient aussi la capacité de solliciter vos prestations », a-t-il fait savoir. De son côté, la marraine, Karidia Sinka/Dramé, s'est également réjouie de la confiance placée en elle pour le lancement de cette initiative sociale. Tout en félicitant les responsables de CAFAS-TOURLET, elle a marqué sa disponibilité à les accompagner dans cette aventure sociale. « Soyez au service de chaque famille avec humilité, rigueur et générosité. Gardez le secret de ceux qui se confient à vous. Protégez les enfants comme vos propres enfants. Restez proches des personnes et de leurs réalités, dans notre pays comme hors de notre pays. La confiance se gagne lentement et, après avoir été éprouvée mille fois, elle se consolide et ne se perd jamais. Restez proches des personnes qui vous contactent », a conseillé la marraine, Karidia Sinka/Dramé. Avec le lancement officiel de ses activités, CAFAS-TOURLET entend ainsi se positionner comme un cadre d'accompagnement et de conseil au service des familles, des couples, des enfants, des jeunes et des personnes âgées, avec pour ambition de contribuer à une société où la famille demeure un espace privilégié d'éducation, de protection et d'épanouissement. Jean-François SOME Minute.bf

items.title: Tougué : parti à la chasse avec un ami, Alsény retrouvé mort dans la commune rurale de Tangaly
items.description: Une découverte macabre a été faite dans la nuit du dimanche au lundi 16 novembre 2026 dans la commune rurale de Tangaly, relevant de la préfecture de Tougué. Alseny Diallo, parti à la chasse avec un ami, a été retrouvé sans vie après plusieurs heures de recherches. Joint au téléphone dans la matinée de ce lundi 16 novembre, Ansoumane Kpoghomou, juge de paix de Tougué, est revenu sur les circonstances de cette découverte. « C’est aux environs de 3 heures du matin que j’ai été appelé par le commandant de la brigade de Tangaly pour m’informer de la nouvelle. Il s’agit d’un certain Alseny Diallo qui était parti à la chasse la veille au soir avec son ami. Ils sont tous les deux chasseurs. Comme c’est leur habitude, ils partent ensemble et se donnent un point de rendez-vous à une heure précise avant de regagner le village. Ce soir-là, chacun avait pris un chemin différent. Lorsque son ami est arrivé au point de rencontre, il ne l’a pas trouvé. Il a essayé de l’appeler au téléphone, mais sans succès. Il a ensuite contacté son épouse pour savoir s’il était rentré, mais celle-ci lui a confirmé que son mari n’était pas encore arrivé », a-t-il expliqué. Après plusieurs heures de recherches, le corps de la victime a finalement été retrouvé. Selon le juge de paix, les premières constatations laissent penser qu’Alseny Diallo aurait fait une chute alors qu’il tentait de rejoindre le point de rendez-vous. « Son ami s’est alors mis à sa recherche. Les circonstances dans lesquelles le corps a été découvert laissent penser qu’il était en train de rejoindre le point de rencontre lorsqu’il est tombé. Son ami et le commandant de la brigade l’ont retrouvé couché sur le ventre, la tête contre le sol, avec sa torche encore allumée à ses côtés. Le commandant a informé le maire et les autorités compétentes, qui se sont rendus sur les lieux aux environs de 3 heures du matin. Ils y sont restés jusqu’à 7 heures », a précisé Ansoumane Kpoghomou. À la suite de l’examen médical du corps, l’hypothèse d’une mort naturelle a été privilégiée, selon le juge de paix. Celui-ci indique toutefois attendre le rapport médical pour déterminer la suite à donner au dossier. « J’avais demandé que le corps soit conservé jusqu’au matin, afin de permettre aux spécialistes de procéder aux examens habituels. Après leur intervention, aucune lésion ni fracture n’a été constatée sur le corps, à l’exception d’une blessure à la tête. Le médecin a conclu à une mort naturelle. J’ai donc ordonné la restitution du corps à la famille pour l’inhumation. J’attends maintenant le rapport du responsable du centre de santé pour voir quelle orientation donner à cette affaire », a-t-il conclu. Alpha Moussa Dieng, correspondant régional à Labé L’article Tougué : parti à la chasse avec un ami, Alsény retrouvé mort dans la commune rurale de Tangaly est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

Ghana Police seek stronger Netherlands partnership on drug and human trafficking
items.description: The Ghana Police Service is strengthening its security cooperation with the Netherlands to tackle human trafficking, drug trafficking, vehicle-related crimes and other transnational offences. The Inspector General of Police (IGP), Christian Tetteh Yohuno, led a delegation of senior police officers in high-level engagements with the Netherlands Police and the leadership of the International Association of Chiefs of Police (IACP) on the sidelines of the IACP 2026 Conference on Monday, October 26. At a meeting with the Chief Constable of the Netherlands Central Police, Yvonne Hondema, discussions focused on expanding bilateral cooperation and strengthening existing partnerships to address cross-border criminal activities. Mr Yohuno highlighted ongoing collaboration between the Netherlands Police, the Netherlands Embassy in Ghana and the International Justice Mission (IJM), particularly in providing training and logistical support to the Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU) and the Anti-Human Trafficking Unit. The meeting also acknowledged the cooperation between the Ghana Police Service, INTERPOL Accra, INTERPOL The Hague and the Netherlands Police Attaché, which resulted in the arrest and deportation of two wanted fugitives to the Netherlands in September 2026. One of the suspects was identified as Richard Danso, who had been the subject of an INTERPOL Red Notice since 2020. The two sides also explored further collaboration in drug trafficking investigations, the application of artificial intelligence in law enforcement, mentorship and logistical support. Proposals included the provision of body cameras and drones to enhance police operations. On vehicle-related crimes, discussions centred on recovering vehicles stolen from the Netherlands and transported to Ghana. The Ghana Police Service disclosed that more than 15 such vehicles had been recovered since September 2025. Ghana was also invited to join the UN Women-supported High-Level Network on Gender-Responsive Policing. At a separate meeting with the IACP leadership, discussions focused on expanding Ghana’s participation in the Association’s international conferences and training programmes. The engagement also explored opportunities for capacity building, technical assistance and the development of policing institutions in Ghana and across Sub-Saharan Africa. The IACP leadership invited the IGP to participate in its conference scheduled for June 26 to 29 in Dublin, Ireland, as part of efforts to deepen international policing cooperation. The engagements form part of the Ghana Police Service’s efforts to strengthen international partnerships, improve information sharing and adopt best practices to enhance its operational capacity. The meetings were attended by members of the Police Management Board (POMAB), including Michael Nketiah Frimpong, DCOP Grace Ansah-Akrofi and the Director of INTERPOL, ACP Naomi Abrebeh Acquah. Also present was Abass Golfrey, FBI Legal Attaché at the United States Embassy in Ghana.

items.title: Oshiomhole tackles Atiku over education privatisation, says Nigeria cannot afford policy
items.description: …challenges Atiku, Obi to clarify education policies ahead of 2027 By Joseph Erunke, Abuja Former Edo State Governor Adams Oshiomhole has taken a swipe at former Vice President Atiku Abubakar over his advocacy for the privatisation of tertiary education, declaring that Nigeria cannot afford to surrender its public education system to private interests when millions of children are still denied access to schooling. Oshiomhole argued that privatising tertiary education would further deepen inequality and undermine access to learning in a country still battling a huge out-of-school population, inadequate educational infrastructure and unequal opportunities. The former governor spoke on Monday in Abuja at the unveiling of the Renewed Hope Education A+Z Scorecard by the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa. He questioned the rationale behind Atiku’s renewed push for private-sector control of tertiary education, recalling that the former Vice-President had pursued a privatisation agenda during his time in office. Oshiomhole also challenged Atiku and former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi to tell Nigerians whether they would sustain or dismantle the education policies introduced by the President Bola Tinubu administration if allowed to govern the country. He insisted that Nigerians deserved clarity on the opposition politicians’ education agenda, particularly on policies designed to expand access to tertiary education and provide financial assistance to students from disadvantaged backgrounds. Taking a further swipe at Atiku, Oshiomhole criticised what he described as the former Vice-President’s position on using public resources to enrich friends, warning that such an approach could undermine critical social investments, particularly education. He maintained that government resources were limited and that decisions on public spending must reflect national priorities rather than personal interests. “If the money he wishes to use to enrich his friends is not diverted to paying student grants, remember that resources are limited at any point in time. That is why economics is about priorities. What is given to those students will not be available to be used to assist friends,” he said. Nigeria’s education crisis remains a major national concern, with millions of children still excluded from formal schooling despite successive government interventions. A 2024 UNICEF estimate put the country’s out-of-school children population at 18.3 million, comprising 10.2 million primary school-age children and 8.1 million children of junior secondary school age, although the Federal Ministry of Education has more recently cited an estimate of about 15 million. Against this backdrop, the federal government has introduced several interventions aimed at expanding access, improving learning outcomes and equipping young Nigerians with employable skills. Among them are the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, the Technical and Vocational Education and Training, TVET, programme, the Nigerian Education Data Infrastructure, NEDI, and targeted interventions to return out-of-school children to classrooms. According to the Federal Ministry of Education’s Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative 2026 report, NELFUND had processed more than 1.65 million applications and disbursed N372.62bn in student loans, covering tuition and upkeep allowances across 319 tertiary institutions. The government also reported that 156,446 verified trainees had benefited from its TVET programme, which offers free vocational training, monthly stipends and start-up support. In a related development, the Federal Government unveiled a National Education Technology Strategy on Monday, aimed at addressing teacher shortages, expanding access to learning and improving education data management through digital platforms. The strategy is expected to bring 26 government initiatives under a coordinated framework covering digital learning, teacher development, education financing and interventions for out-of-school children. Earlier, Alausa disclosed that the federal government had put funding arrangements in place for its education data infrastructure, while introducing a three-year renegotiation window in its agreement with the Academic Staff Union of Universities and other university-based unions. He explained that the provision would allow the agreements to be reviewed every three years, providing a mechanism for addressing staff welfare and remuneration concerns before they escalate into prolonged industrial disputes. The federal government had in October unveiled fresh agreements with academic and non-academic staff unions in tertiary institutions, featuring improved welfare packages, allowances and a monitoring framework to ensure implementation. The three-year review arrangement is also expected to strengthen regular engagement between the government and university unions and minimise recurring strikes that have repeatedly disrupted academic calendars. The Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Sa’id Ahmad, said the ministry was also pursuing reforms to strengthen governance and discipline in educational institutions. She listed the introduction of guidelines for appointing vice-chancellors, rectors and provosts, alongside policies addressing bullying in schools, among measures being implemented to improve standards across the education sector. Cette initiative environnementale réunit les représentants de la société civile, les unités de la protection civile ainsi que les habitants de la région, tous mobilisés autour d'un objectif commun, précise encore la même source en soulignat que l'opération vise ainsi à renforcer durablement le couvert végétal, à lutter contre l'érosion des sols et à préserver la richesse de l'écosystème local. items.title: Tinubu’s education reforms reach 3m tertiary students, Alausa tells opposition
items.description: …Accuses opposition of misleading Nigerians, says government prioritising results over promises By Joseph Erunke, Abuja Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, has challenged opposition politicians, particularly former Labour Party presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to familiarise themselves with Nigeria’s education laws before criticising the Federal Government’s policies, insisting that nearly three million tertiary students are benefiting from President Bola Tinubu’s reforms. Alausa, who accused the opposition of deliberately misrepresenting the administration’s interventions, said criticisms of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, and other education policies were misplaced and failed to acknowledge the benefits Nigerians were already enjoying. The minister fired back at Obi on Monday during a briefing at the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council headquarters in Abuja, where he defended the Tinubu administration’s record in education ahead of the 2027 general elections. In a direct response to Obi’s criticisms, Alausa said the former presidential candidate needed to study the relevant legislation before making public statements about the government’s education financing arrangements. “What Mr Obi is saying is borne out of ignorance. He needs to read the law. This is the law of Nigeria,” the minister declared. He further accused Obi of misleading Nigerians, saying: “If Mr Obi wants to blame me and mislead the public and Nigerians, that tells you the kind of person he is.” At the centre of the disagreement is the four per cent development levy introduced under the Nigeria Tax Act, which Alausa said was designed to guarantee sustainable funding for the student loan scheme. He explained that 15 per cent of the proceeds from the levy was earmarked for NELFUND, insisting that the allocation was expressly provided for in the law and not an arbitrary government arrangement. The minister challenged Obi to examine the relevant provisions of the legislation rather than cast doubts on the funding structure of the scheme. Defending the broader education reforms, Alausa said the administration’s interventions had expanded access to tertiary education through student loans, improved infrastructure, increased funding and efforts to address the shortage of academic personnel in universities and other higher institutions. He disclosed that nearly three million students in tertiary institutions and another 200,000 students in secondary schools had benefited from the administration’s interventions. “We have almost three million Nigerian students in tertiary education and another 200,000 in secondary education. Today, students in every single section of our country have benefited the most from President Tinubu’s transformative agenda,” he said. Rejecting what he described as an opposition fixation on policy announcements, Alausa argued that the real measure of government performance should be the tangible benefits reaching Nigerians rather than promises and political rhetoric. “We have enough policies in Nigeria. We want tangible benefits for Nigerians. So, every single thing about today is not about policies. What I am trying to tell you is how Nigerians are benefiting,” he said. Beyond student financing, the minister disclosed that the Federal Government had developed guidelines to strengthen governance in universities, particularly in the appointment of vice-chancellors, while committees had been established to monitor compliance. He also identified efforts to tackle bullying in schools and ensure that recommendations from previous education review panels were implemented before another round of policy reviews commenced. Alausa’s defence comes amid mounting opposition criticism of the administration’s education spending and reform priorities. Obi had in July faulted the Federal Government’s decision to phase out the policy separating junior and senior secondary schools, arguing that Nigeria’s education challenges were rooted in inadequate funding, poor management and weak leadership rather than the structure of the school system. The former Anambra governor also criticised the 2026 education budget, claiming that the sector received only 6.17 per cent of total expenditure, far below UNESCO’s recommended 15 to 20 per cent benchmark. However, the Tinubu administration has continued to defend its education agenda, pointing to interventions in basic education, technical and vocational training, digital learning, teacher development and tertiary education financing. Figures released by the Federal Government showed that NELFUND had disbursed N372.62bn in student loans across 319 tertiary institutions, covering tuition and upkeep allowances. The administration has also introduced programmes targeting out-of-school children, expanded technical education opportunities and pursued digital initiatives to improve education planning and service delivery. With the 2027 general elections approaching, education has increasingly become a battleground between the ruling APC and opposition politicians, with the government relying on its reform record to justify its quest for another mandate. The post Tinubu’s education reforms reach 3m tertiary students, Alausa tells opposition appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Accra summit makes the case for African culture in the Culture Global Stocktake
items.description: The Climate x Culture Summit in Accra opened with an acoustic performance by EliThreeSixty. Later in the programme, a live band from the Restoration Artistes Network took the stage with music celebrating environmental restoration and speaking against galamsey. It was an unusual way to approach a climate conference, but that was precisely the point. At the October 22 gathering, music and creative expression were not just entertainment around the discussions. They were part of the conversation about how to get people to understand climate change and take action. Organised by CultureJoint Media in partnership with the Office of the Minister of State for Climate Change and Sustainability at the Presidency, the summit brought together artists, policymakers, environmental advocates, researchers, event organisers and financial institutions under the theme “Designing Sustainable Creative Experiences for Africa.” The discussions ranged from waste management at concerts and festivals to the financing of creative businesses, the preservation of indigenous knowledge and the use of storytelling to influence public behaviour. They also came ahead of the launch of the Culture Global Stocktake (CGST) at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, on November 10. The civil-society-led initiative seeks to make the case for culture to be better recognised and integrated into global climate policy, including the UNFCCC’s Second Global Stocktake. Although the Accra summit was not part of the formal CGST process, several of the issues raised there speak to the initiative’s wider concern: how cultural practices, local knowledge and creative industries can contribute to climate action. Delivering a keynote on behalf of the Minister of State for Climate Change and Sustainability, the Office’s Head of Administration, Ruth Dzokoto, said music, film, fashion and storytelling could help translate complex climate issues into messages people could relate to. “Culture can make climate action visible, relatable, and desirable,” she said. But the summit did not stop at the power of communication. Cultural entrepreneur Ruddy Kwakye challenged event organisers to examine the environmental cost of the festivals, concerts and other experiences they produce. He proposed a six-point Green Stage Plan built around measuring waste and energy use, reducing single-use materials, working with waste pickers, restoring event grounds, controlling noise and cutting unnecessary energy consumption. “The cheapest rubbish to clean up is the rubbish that never comes in,” he said, making the case for refill points, reusable cups and better control of packaging before guests even arrive. The plan also called for waste pickers and aggregators to be hired and paid for their work, arguing that waste management could support livelihoods while reducing the environmental impact of events. That conversation has implications for Ghana’s own climate commitments. Its updated Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) under the Paris Agreement sets out 47 adaptation and mitigation programmes for the 2020–2030 period. The priorities include sustainable energy, landscape restoration, waste management, climate resilience and responsible production and consumption. The summit explored how the creative industry could contribute to some of these targets, from reducing plastic waste and energy use at events to using cultural platforms to promote restoration and climate-conscious behaviour. The connection was raised directly during the panel on greening Ghana’s events and creative industry. Energy researcher and policy analyst Benjamin Nsiah urged creative businesses to pay attention to national climate frameworks when planning their operations. “If you are talking greening and you want to include that or integrate that in our activities as creatives, what data are we using?” he asked, referring to the NDCs and other national policy documents. His point was that sustainability should not be reduced to a slogan or a branding exercise. Organisers need to know what they are trying to change and use relevant data to measure progress. The discussion on landscape restoration brought another dimension to the relationship between culture and climate action. Eric Lartey of the World Resources Institute outlined work under its Restore Local initiative, which supports locally led restoration in Ghana’s cocoa-growing landscapes. He argued that restoration efforts were more likely to last when communities had a say in how their land was managed and their knowledge was taken seriously. “Local leadership is not simply a nice addition to restoration, but it is essential to its sustainability,” he said. The Restoration Artistes Network performance that followed carried the subject into music, using songs about restoration and the threat of illegal mining to give the issue a different kind of public expression. Musician Okyeame Kwame also urged artists to pay more attention to indigenous practices that have traditionally helped communities protect their environment. He cited sacred groves in the Ashanti Region and the Volta Region, where songs and drum language were used to warn against encroachment. In one account from his research in the Volta Region, he said the last person who knew a particular song used to alert the community had died without the knowledge being recorded. “The last person that knew the song was a woman, and she had died, and it wasn’t documented,” he said. For him, artists and content creators have a role in documenting such knowledge and finding ways to bring it into contemporary music, film, poetry and digital storytelling. Valerie Kplorm Nutakor of the Climate and Development Knowledge Network (CDKN) made a related point about the need to measure whether climate communication actually changes behaviour. She shared an example from a project in the Upper West Region where women produced songs in local languages to communicate climate information. The project examined whether the messages influenced farming practices, including tree cutting, replanting and the use of natural fertilisers. “You always have to have the key indicators outlined before you even do the communication,” she said. The summit also turned to a familiar problem for artists and creative businesses: access to finance. Eva Ackuaku, Head of Sustainable Financing and Impact at CBG Bank Ghana, said banks needed to see proper documentation, research and a clear business case before financing projects. Environmental benefits alone, she explained, were not enough to make a project commercially viable. “As much as it might have environmental and social benefits, we also make sure that the business makes commercial sense,” she said. Multimedia Group data analyst Isaac Kofi Agyei said the creative sector needed better records and more reliable data to help financial institutions understand the businesses they were being asked to support. “It’s not just about good intent, but it’s also about good data,” he said. On the events industry, Peter Ansah of Republic of Amusement acknowledged that there was still considerable work to be done. “We are not green enough, to be very frank,” he said, pointing to the need for event organisers, sponsors and other partners to share the responsibility and risks involved in adopting more sustainable practices. The final panel looked at storytelling and artificial intelligence. Performance poet and playwright Chief Moomen said artists needed to be equipped with the knowledge to handle climate issues in their work, but warned against turning creative content into a lecture. “The job of the artist, for example, is to take complex information and break it down into emotionally appealing content,” he said. For CultureJoint Media, the summit is part of a wider effort to connect African arts, culture and the creative economy with conversations about climate, technology and development. The proposed Accra Climate Culture Accord and Sustainable Event Production Guide for Ghana are among the intended outcomes of the gathering. The work ahead will be to turn the discussions into practical partnerships and measurable changes in the way creative businesses and events operate. It will also mean making a stronger case for the creative sector’s place in Ghana’s climate planning. As the Culture Global Stocktake takes the case for culture into the international climate conversation, the experience in Accra offers a Ghanaian perspective: climate action can take shape in policy rooms, but it can also begin on a stage, in a song, in a community’s memory and in the choices made by the people organising the next big event. The author, Kenneth Awotwe Darko, is a culture journalist, climate activist and founder of Climate x Culture Summit.

items.title: Labé : pris pour un malade mental en raison de son mode de vie, un vendeur de charbon possède huit motos et 38 millions GNF
items.description: Une découverte pour le moins surprenante alimente les conversations dans la cité de Karamoko Alpha mo Labé. Huit motos et une somme estimée à 38 millions de francs guinéens ont été retrouvées au domicile d’un vendeur de charbon, installé depuis plusieurs années au secteur Kourahodé, dans le quartier Konkola, relevant de la commune urbaine de Labé. La découverte est intervenue à la suite d’un préavis de départ adressé par le propriétaire de la maison à son locataire. C’est dans le cadre de cette procédure que des agents de l’escadron mobile de gendarmerie de Labé, accompagnés du chef de secteur de Kourahodé, ont effectué une perquisition au domicile de l’intéressé. Selon les informations recueillies, le comportement et le mode de vie de cet homme avaient longtemps suscité des interrogations dans son entourage. Régulièrement aperçu dans des vêtements sales et laissant traîner ses habits un peu partout dans la maison, il était considéré par certains comme une personne souffrant de troubles mentaux. Une perception qui, à ce stade, ne repose toutefois sur aucun diagnostic médical connu. Mais la fouille de sa chambre a réservé une véritable surprise aux personnes présentes. Derrière les conditions de vie particulièrement désordonnées du locataire, les agents ont découvert huit motos ainsi qu’une importante somme d’argent, estimée à 38 millions de francs guinéens. Interrogé sur les circonstances de cette découverte, Moustapha Baldé, chef de secteur de Kourahodé, est revenu sur le déroulement des faits. « C’est un citoyen qui réside dans mon secteur depuis des années. Il exerce le commerce de charbon depuis 2003. Lors de la perquisition, nous avons d’abord découvert des habits sales avant de tomber sur huit motos et une somme estimée à 38 millions de francs guinéens », a-t-il expliqué. D’après le responsable local, les vérifications effectuées ont permis de constater que les huit motos sont immatriculées au nom du vendeur de charbon. L’argent retrouvé lui appartiendrait également. Selon les explications recueillies, il aurait constitué progressivement cette épargne grâce aux revenus de son activité commerciale. Moustapha Baldé précise par ailleurs que le propriétaire de la maison aurait engagé la procédure de préavis après avoir constaté l’accumulation de déchets et le désordre entretenu par son locataire dans la concession. Des arriérés de loyer remontant à trois ans auraient également été évoqués par les propriétaires, une accusation qui reste toutefois à établir. À la suite de cette découverte, les responsables présents auraient envisagé de faire le point sur les éventuels loyers impayés, de procéder à leur règlement sur présentation de justificatifs et de restituer au locataire le reliquat de son argent ainsi que ses motos. Aux dernières nouvelles, les deux parties se trouvaient toujours dans les locaux de l’escadron mobile de gendarmerie de Labé, dans l’espoir de trouver une issue amiable à cette affaire. Cette découverte met en lumière le parcours atypique d’un commerçant qui, malgré un mode de vie ayant alimenté les préjugés de son entourage, aurait réussi à constituer un patrimoine important au fil de plus de vingt années d’activité dans la vente de charbon. Alpha Moussa Dieng, correspondant régional à Labé L’article Labé : pris pour un malade mental en raison de son mode de vie, un vendeur de charbon possède huit motos et 38 millions GNF est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: At ECO moot, Dar calls for translating 'collective commitments into concrete action'
items.description: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar closed out the 30th meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) Council of Ministers (COM) in Islamabad on Monday with a call for countries to translate their commitments into action. Pakistan, which holds the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27, hosted the meeting under the theme “Reviving Regionalism for a Resilient ECO”. The deputy premier, who chaired the meeting, expressed his “sincere appreciation to all delegations” for their constructive engagement during the meeting. “The deliberations today have reaffirmed our shared commitment to regional economic cooperation and integration,” Dar said. He termed the adoption of the Strategic Goals of Economic Cooperation 2035 an “important milestone in charting the future course of our organisation over the next decade”, saying that it provided a shared framework to advance regional priorities alongside the Islamabad Communiqué. “Our task now is to translate our collective commitments into concrete action,” he added. “This will require clear priorities, realistic timelines, and effective follow-up mechanisms.” He highlighted regional cooperation as a central pillar of Pakistan’s foreign policy and noted that the country had consistently advocated a “stronger, more effective and responsive” ECO that harnessed “geographical proximity, historical bonds and economic complementarities”. Dar underscored Pakistan’s commitment to advancing the ECO agenda as the chair of the organisation and to working with all institutions and member states to strengthen regional connectivity, facilitate intra-regional trade and promote mutually beneficial economic cooperation. He looked forward to welcoming the countries back for the 31st COM meeting in 2027, saying, “Let us build on the momentum generated here so that our next meeting can take stock of tangible progress in advancing our shared priorities.” In addition, he wished Iran success in hosting the upcoming 18th ECO summit on Dec 3-4. The deputy premier thanked all member states, as well as the secretary general and his team, ECO permanent representatives, and senior officials for their support. Later in the day, Dar held a media briefing on the meeting alongside ECO Secretary General Asad Majeed Khan and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar. Joint communiqué The COM meeting concluded with the adoption of two documents, including the Strategic Goals of Economic Cooperation 2035 and the Islamabad Communiqué. Pakistan’s mediation efforts hailed In the Islamabad Communiqué, ECO member states expressed concern over the “challenging geopolitical environment in the region, emphasising the importance of restraint, dialogue and diplomatic engagement, and recognising the important role” of Iran as a founding member of ECO. They expressed support for the mediation efforts undertaken by Pakistan and Qatar, as well as for the recent initiative put forward by Iran “aimed at achieving a dignified resolution of the conflict and ensuring the complete and permanent termination of the current war”. The ECO states commended Pakistan’s “consistent and constructive diplomatic support for ECO Member States and its mediation efforts towards de-escalation during the recent Iran-United States crisis”. They reaffirmed the importance of dialogue, diplomacy, respect for international law and promoting mutual trust. stability and the peaceful resolution of disputes, and calling for continued cooperation within the ECO framework towards lasting peace and stability in the region. The communiqué also highly appreciated Qatar’s “important role as a trusted facilitator of international diplomacy, most notably demonstrated by its mediation efforts at the 81st United Nations General Assembly”. The members commended ECO for “demonstrating that regionalism can remain effective and operational even under conditions of acute geopolitical stress”. The meeting expressed support for various documents adopted in the past, including ECO Vision 2025 and 2021 Ashgabat Consensus for Action. They also welcomed various UN resolutions and initiatives. Araghchi calls for sustainable energy mechanism At the ECO meeting, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stressed the need for a reliable and sustainable regional energy mechanism during his address. The Iranian FM spoke about the US-Israeli war on Iran , which has also resulted in the choking of key fuel supply routes — the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab . “Our region needs not only an independent security framework but also a reliable and sustainable regional energy mechanism to safeguard energy flows, ensure stable supplies, reduce external vulnerabilities and enhance collective resilience against geopolitical shocks and disruptions,” Araghchi said, according to a transcript of his speech provided by the Iranian embassy in Pakistan. Araghchi said ECO was moving “beyond its traditional role towards becoming an effective platform for collective action, strengthened cooperation and joint efforts”. He said the shift would enable member states “to address emerging challenges and contribute to an inclusive and equitable global economic order”. He stressed the need for a “modern, new-generation, more inclusive, effective and operational trade agreement” that would benefit the region. Referring to the US war on Iran, Araghchi said, “Iran has remained committed to diplomatic engagement and peaceful solutions.” He added, however, that the US had opted for a different course of action, which was “marked by aggression, threats, targeted assassinations, economic coercion, and blockades, in flagrant violation of international law and the UN Charter”. He underscored that Iran had “no inherent dispute” with countries in the region, adding that “the territories, airspace and facilities of the regional countries must not be used as platforms for launching attacks against each other”. “Iran’s legitimate defensive measures are directed exclusively at the targets and military bases of the aggressors and should in no way be construed as actions against the peoples or governments of the neighbouring countries,” Araghchi said. He also called attention to Palestine , describing the genocide in Gaza as “the most pressing international crisis”. Condemning the destruction and killings at the hands of Israeli forces in Palestine, he said, “We are witnessing the intensification of expansionist policies by the Israeli regime in the West Bank and occupied Al-Quds.” “This is a moment that calls for concrete action, collective responsibility, and an end to silence and indifference.” He concluded his speech by reiterating that Iran’s stability and prosperity were “intrinsically linked” to those of other ECO members. ECO delegation heads call on PM Shehbaz Separately, the foreign ministers and delegation heads of ECO member states paid a joint call on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, according to a handout issued by the PM’s Office. The premier thanked them for their participation in the meeting and reaffirmed Pakistan’s “strong commitment” to ECO objectives. He reiterated his government’s resolve to promote regional cooperation, connectivity and economic integration within the ECO member states. The premier appreciated the meeting’s successful conclusion and welcomed the adoption of the Islamabad Communique and the Strategic Goals of Economic Cooperation 2035, describing them as “important steps” towards strengthening the organisation and advancing shared regional priorities. The premier highlighted Pakistan’s ECO chairmanship and emphasised the need to translate the organisation’s collective vision into concrete, result-oriented initiatives that deliver “tangible benefits” to the region’s people. Furthermore, the handout said that the premier called for enhanced cooperation in trade and investment, transport and transit connectivity, energy, information and communication technology, and sustainable development. “He stressed the importance of effective implementation of existing ECO agreements and strengthening institutional mechanisms to accelerate regional economic integration,” the statement said. PM Shehbaz highlighted the country’s strategic geographical location. He reiterated Pakistan’s commitment to enhancing regional connectivity through road, rail and multimodal transport corridors, including linkages with the ports of Karachi, Port Qasim and Gwadar, to facilitate access to regional and international markets, particularly for landlocked ECO member states. “Underlining Pakistan’s commitment to dialogue and diplomacy for the peaceful resolution of disputes, the premier stressed the importance of collective efforts to address threats to regional security,” the statement added. He also expressed Pakistan’s resolve to work closely with all member states and the ECO secretariat to further strengthen the organisation during its chairmanship. “The prime minister reaffirmed that Pakistan looked forward to welcoming ECO member states again in 2027 for the next Council of Ministers Meeting and the ECO summit,” the handout concluded. Dar holds sideline meetings with participating dignitaries The deputy premier also held separate meetings with ministers from several countries attending the ECO moot. With FM Araghchi , Dar emphasised that dialogue and diplomacy remain the only viable means of addressing outstanding issues, preventing escalation and achieving lasting peace and stability, the Foreign Office said. Meanwhile, Tajikistan’s FM Sirojiddin Muhriddin and Dar reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation within ECO and advancing its regional priorities. According to FO, the Tajik minister appreciated Pakistan’s warm hospitality. The two leaders “underscored the importance of realising the full potential of bilateral trade” and also discussed advancing energy cooperation, particularly through the early operationalisation of CASA-1000 . Dar and Turkiye’s Deputy FM Musa Kulaklikaya reaffirmed their “commitment to further strengthening the longstanding bonds of friendship and brotherhood” between their countries, FO said. Dar thanked Türkiye for its active participation in the Council of Ministers meeting, while Kulaklikaya thanked Pakistan for the warm hospitality and arrangements for the meeting. In his meeting with Dar, Kyrgyz Republic’s Deputy FM Kairat Tursunkulov delivered a letter from Foreign Minister Zheenbek Kulubaev, “reaffirming the close bonds of friendship and commitment to advancing bilateral ties”, FO said. The two sides discussed strengthening bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade and connectivity, and emphasised the importance of continued cooperation under ECO. Pakistan calls on Afghanistan to address terror concerns In his opening speech at the meeting, Dar said Pakistan desired a peaceful, prosperous and stable Afghanistan , but meaningful progress towards regional cooperation required the Afghan authorities to address the legitimate security concerns of neighbouring countries, particularly the threat of terrorism. He added that a stable Afghanistan, at peace with itself and all its neighbours and fully integrated into the ECO framework, would benefit the Afghan people as well as the wider region by opening up avenues for trade, transit and economic cooperation. “At the same time, meaningful progress requires the Afghan authorities to address the legitimate security concerns of the neighbouring countries, particularly the threat of terrorism,” Dar said. He stressed that a secure and stable environment was essential for sustained regional economic partnerships, adding that these considerations remained central to Pakistan’s broader connectivity agenda. “Regional connectivity rests on more than the routes that link us. It depends upon trust between states and confidence that international commitments will be honoured. Unresolved disputes and the non-fulfilment of international obligations can erode that trust and impede economic progress,” said Dar. The foreign minister emphasised that respect for international law and treaties is essential to enduring economic partnerships between countries. Outlining Pakistan’s priorities during its chairmanship of the ECO, Dar identified five key areas of focus, including expanding trade and investment, strengthening regional connectivity, advancing the ECO Trade Agreement, building regional resilience and promoting human development. The foreign minister said the region’s natural resources, energy reserves, agricultural potential and strategic location offered considerable opportunities for economic cooperation, but realising that potential required functioning transport corridors, efficient border procedures and predictable transit arrangements. He said Pakistan would work towards wider market access, stronger regional value chains and greater private sector participation, particularly by small and medium-sized enterprises, to boost trade and investment among member states. “Closer interaction among our business communities can help translate commercial potential into greater trade and investment.” Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar in a cordial exchange with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, Tajikistan Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Muhriddin, OIC Secretary General Ismail Ould Cheikh Ahmed and ECO Secretary General Dr. Asad Majeed Khan on the sidelines of the 30th ECO Council of Ministers Meeting in Islamabad on Nov 16. — ForeignOfficePk/X On connectivity, Dar said Pakistan would seek to improve transport and transit links between Central Asia, South Asia and Pakistani ports on the Arabian Sea. Harmonised customs procedures, efficient border management and predictable transit arrangements were essential to making regional trade routes commercially viable, he added. The foreign minister also highlighted the need to advance the ECO Trade Agreement, saying the negotiating strategy and roadmap approved by ECO trade ministers in November 2025 provided a basis for modernising the agreement. Pakistan would support efforts to develop a more effective, inclusive and digitally enabled regional trade framework, he said. On regional resilience, Dar called for closer cooperation in disaster preparedness, early warning systems, sustainable water management and climate-resilient infrastructure, noting that climate change and growing pressure on water and energy resources posed serious challenges to regional economies. He also underscored the importance of human development, particularly in education, research, innovation and vocational training, saying greater opportunities in these areas could equip young people with skills needed by changing economies. Promoting entrepreneurship and professional exchanges would further strengthen regional integration, he added. The foreign minister maintained that the five priorities were interconnected and their success would depend on collective efforts by member states. He expressed Pakistan’s readiness to work with ECO members and the organisation’s secretariat on initiatives relating to trade facilitation, transit connectivity and disaster preparedness. Regional peace and diplomatic efforts Dar cautioned that peace and stability were essential for economic development, warning that conflict and insecurity in the region could disrupt trade routes, energy supplies, investment and economic projects. “Peace and development reinforce each other,” he said. He added that Pakistan remained “deeply concerned about conflict and instability” in the region. “Their consequences extend beyond national boundaries, disrupting trade routes, energy supplies, investment, and the economic projects of our peoples.” He said that Pakistan has consistently advocated for “the peaceful resolution of disputes through dialogue and diplomacy in accordance with international law and the United Nations Charter”. Referring to Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts in the US-Israeli war on Iran, Dar said, “Pakistan will continue these diplomatic efforts in support of dialogue, de-escalation, and lasting regional stability.” He said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir “remained closely engaged with brotherly countries and international partners to facilitate peaceful outcomes”. Senior officials meet to finalise agenda Senior officials of the ECO finalised the agenda and draft Islamabad Communiqué on Sunday, ahead of the organisation’s COM meeting. According to a statement issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA), the Senior Officials Meeting (SOM) was held on Nov 15 under the chairmanship of Foreign Secretary Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad. The meeting was attended by senior officials from ECO member states, representatives of the ECO Secretariat, and delegates from the organisation’s specialised agencies and regional institutions. The officials reviewed preparations for the ministerial meeting and finalised its agenda and the draft Islamabad Communiqué for consideration by the foreign ministers. They also reviewed the activities undertaken by the ECO Secretariat during the year, including ongoing programmes and initiatives, outcomes of sectoral ministerial meetings, and the work of subsidiary bodies and specialised institutions, the ministry said. Administrative and financial matters of the organisation also came under discussion, with participants exchanging views on measures to improve its effectiveness. The SOM serves as a preparatory forum for the ECO COM, enabling member states to assess progress, discuss issues of mutual interest and build consensus on proposals and draft documents ahead of ministerial-level deliberations.

Asiedu Nketiah urges police to investigate alleged vote-buying in NDC regional elections
items.description: The National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, has called on the Ghana Police Service to investigate allegations of vote-buying during the party’s recently concluded regional elections and prosecute persons found culpable. The call follows reports that some delegates were allegedly given cash, household appliances and vehicles in exchange for votes in the contest for various party positions. The allegations have raised concerns within the governing party, attracting the attention of its national leadership amid questions about the growing monetisation of internal party elections. Speaking on the matter, Mr Nketiah said that while there was nothing inherently wrong with party members receiving gifts, the practice becomes unacceptable when used to influence electoral outcomes. “It is not a bad thing if anybody wants to give party people something. But if it happens in a way around elections to suggest that we are just buying positions, then it is not acceptable at all in a democracy,” he said. He stressed that alleged vote-buying should not be treated solely as an internal party disciplinary matter, particularly where the conduct may amount to a criminal offence. According to him, the police and other state security institutions must be prepared to investigate and take appropriate action regardless of the political party involved. “Once you are citizens and we are all subject to the laws of this country, when you want to subordinate the national laws to party laws, that’s not correct. Then you are part of the problem,” he stated. Read also: NDC Ashanti election: Delegates receive fridges, TVs, blenders and cash Mr Nketiah urged the security services to act on any evidence of conduct that violates the country’s criminal laws, insisting that political affiliation should not shield offenders from prosecution. “The security services should be bold to proceed with whatever measures they want to do the same way as they deal with crime anywhere else,” he added. He further said that state investigations and possible prosecutions should take precedence over internal party disciplinary processes where criminality is suspected. The NDC National Chairman acknowledged that the party leadership had a responsibility to enforce its internal rules and caution members against electoral malpractice but maintained that party regulations were not sufficient to address criminal conduct. “We in party leadership have our responsibility to caution, to apply the party laws. But the party laws are not strong enough to deal with crime,” he said. He cautioned against a situation where state institutions would hesitate to investigate alleged wrongdoing simply because it involves members of a particular political party. He said the police should not wait for the leadership of either the NDC or the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP) to take action before performing their constitutional duties.

items.title: Gov’t will provide funds to EXIM Bank for on-lending to the tree crop sector – President Mahama
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama has announced plans to provide funding to the Ghana Export-Import Bank (Ghana EXIM Bank) to support financing for Ghana’s cashew industry as part of government’s New Economy agenda. He said the intervention would enable the bank to provide financial support to cashew processors to purchase adequate quantities of raw nuts and sustain their operations throughout the year. Speaking at the commissioning of NADKANSCO Cashew Processing Limited in Techiman on Monday, November 16, 2026, President Mahama said cashew production and processing formed part of the government’s broader investment priorities under the agribusiness and tree crops sectors. “So as part of the new economy, like I said, we are devoting money for agribusiness. And in agribusiness, the tree crops sector is included. And so cashew is a part of the new economy,” he said. He added: “We will lend money to Ghana EXIM to on-lend to NADKANSCO so that NADKANSCO can acquire enough cashew nuts to process throughout the year.” The announcement follows the presentation of the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy, which is anchored on the government’s New Economy agenda. President Mahama said the broader objective was to strengthen the entire cashew value chain by supporting local processors to secure raw materials, expand production and create sustainable employment. He noted that inadequate working capital remained a major challenge for processing companies, making it difficult for them to purchase and preserve enough raw cashew nuts to maintain production outside the harvesting season. Using NADKANSCO as an example, he said the factory’s available working capital could sustain operations for only about 60 to 80 days, despite its capacity to process between 30,000 and 31,000 metric tonnes annually. The President said government wanted to prevent local processing factories from shutting down after the harvesting season and ensure they provided employment throughout the year. He also announced plans to restrict raw cashew exports during the first three months of the harvesting season to give local processors priority in purchasing the commodity. Additionally, government intends to introduce a levy on raw cashew exports, with proceeds channelled into a fund to support local processing companies. The measures, he said, would help retain more value from Ghana’s cashew production, strengthen domestic processing capacity and create jobs under the New Economy agenda.

items.title: Two mass shootings claim 17 lives in South Africa
items.description: By Juliet Umeh, Agency Report At least 17 people have been killed in two separate mass shootings in South Africa, with police yet to establish the motives behind the attacks, which occurred about 530 kilometres apart on Sunday. Eight people were found dead inside a bullet-riddled vehicle in Sweetwaters, outside Pietermaritzburg, while nine others were killed in a shack in Jeffsville, near the capital, Pretoria. Police spokesperson, Robert Netshiunda, said the identities of the eight victims in Sweetwaters were yet to be confirmed, although some families had approached authorities to assist. “It’s still too early to tell what the motive could have been and who could be behind the shooting because we are yet to identify the victims,” he said. In Jeffsville, six males and three females were found with gunshot wounds inside a four-room shack. Police spokesperson, Brenda Muridili, said officers were alerted at about 7:30 a.m. on Monday, although the shooting reportedly occurred between 10 p.m. and 11 p.m. on Sunday. No arrests had been made as investigations continued. Gauteng Police Commissioner, Tommy Mthombeni, said the killings could be linked to a shooting in nearby Saulsville last year, which claimed 12 lives and left 13 others injured. He disclosed that one of Sunday’s victims was a person of interest in the previous attack, adding that police could not rule out retaliation. South Africa has recorded several deadly mass shootings in the past year. In September, 11 people, including a pregnant woman, were killed in an attack on a house near Durban, while another shooting at a tavern claimed 17 lives. Two separate shootings in Johannesburg in June also left 24 people dead, with police linking one to rival illegal mining gangs. Two other mass shootings in December last year claimed 21 lives. Police investigations into Sunday’s attacks are ongoing. The post Two mass shootings claim 17 lives in South Africa appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nigeria’s inflation rate drops to 14.06% in October
items.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan Nigeria’s headline inflation rate declined to 14.06 per cent in October 2026 from 14.63 per cent recorded in September, the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) has said. The NBS disclosed this in its latest Consumer Price Index (CPI) report released on Monday, also showing a decline in food inflation to 19.13 per cent in October from 19.59 per cent in the preceding month. According to the report, headline inflation stood at 18.97 per cent in October 2025, indicating a 4.91 percentage-point decline in the annual rate between October 2025 and October 2026. The statistics agency, however, reported an increase in the month-on-month headline inflation rate, which rose to 0.43 per cent in October from 0.06 per cent in September. It explained that the development indicated that the average price level increased at a faster rate in October than in the preceding month. “In October 2026, the Headline inflation rate stood at 14.06%, down from 14.63% in September 2026 and stood at 18.97% in the same month of the preceding year (October 2025),” the NBS stated. The report added that the October 2026 headline inflation rate represented a 4.91 percentage-point decline compared with the corresponding period of the previous year. “On a month-on-month basis, the Headline inflation rate in October 2026 was 0.43%, which was 0.38% higher than the rate recorded in September 2026 (0.06%). “This means that in October 2026, the rate of increase in the average price level was higher than the rate of increase in the average price level in September 2026,” the agency said. items.title: INEC disowns ‘staff’ behind report of partisan recruitment in Edo
items.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Edo has disowned the author of a viral video, claiming to have recruited ad-hoc personnel for the commission and directing them to work for a particular political interest. In a statement issued on Monday in Benin by the commission’s Head of Voter Education and Publicity, Mr Samuel Sunday, on behalf of the Resident Electoral Commissioner, the commission stated that the man was not its staff member. “INEC Edo declares that no one named Osayi Israel Omoroduwa is among its staff in Edo, and that no one has the power or access to recruit ad-hoc staff for the commission,” Sunday explained. He further explained that the recruitment of ad-hoc personnel was conducted exclusively through the online INECPRES platform, administered by INEC Headquarters. “The path to being an ad-hoc staff of INEC is by online application through the INECPRES platform and whoever has internet access can do so by themselves or support others so qualified to apply,” he added. He emphasised that staff members in its state offices could not influence the recruitment process, adding that the person named in the video had no special access to the platform. According to Sunday, successful applicants will undergo scrutiny by the commission and receive training on the conduct and ethics of elections. The INEC Spokesman described the online video as “an irresponsible and targeted attack” on the commission and its processes. He argued that the video was intended to undermine public confidence in the electoral process through misinformation. He, however, reaffirmed the commitment of the commission to conducting credible elections and urged the public to disregard what it described as “falsehood contained in the video”. (NAN) The post INEC disowns ‘staff’ behind report of partisan recruitment in Edo appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: We blocked channels used to siphon Abia funds — Otti
items.description: Governor attributes poor roads, dirty environment to alleged diversion of public resources By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, has attributed the infrastructural and environmental challenges inherited by his administration to the alleged diversion of public resources by some politicians in the state. Otti said his administration had blocked entrenched channels through which public funds were allegedly siphoned, describing the former system as a political feeding bottle. The governor, who spoke at a two-day crusade organised by the Lord’s Chosen Charismatic Renewal Ministries at Ogbonnaya Onu Polytechnic, Aba, said those criticising his administration were unhappy because they could no longer access public resources through the alleged channels. “Why they are murmuring is that we removed the feeding bottle from their mouths. And that feeding bottle was what they used to siphon all our resources. That was why there were no good roads and everywhere was dirty,” he said. Otti maintained that his administration would not reverse course despite criticisms, insisting that blocking access to public resources by vested interests was necessary to redirect government funds towards development. He cited road rehabilitation, improved environmental sanitation and drainage infrastructure in Aba as evidence of the changes recorded under his administration. According to him, the city has witnessed significant improvement in flood control, with floodwaters no longer lingering after heavy rainfall as they reportedly did in previous years. “Before now, there were no good roads, everywhere was dirty, the gutters were blocked, and whenever it rained, the entire place became flooded. “But I am sure that those of you living in Aba can testify that, despite the heavy rains this year, floodwaters no longer remain for long after the rains,” he said. Promises consolidation after rescue phase Looking ahead, Otti said the achievements recorded in the past three and a half years represented only the beginning of his administration’s efforts to reposition the state. He promised that the next four and a half years would focus on consolidating the gains already recorded. “What we have done in three and a half years is just the beginning of the rescue. The next four and a half years will be serious consolidation,” he declared. The governor also announced plans to improve facilities for future large-scale crusades organised by the ministry following concerns over the exposure of worshippers to the scorching sun at the polytechnic venue. He disclosed that he had directed the Commissioner for Youth and Sports Development to ensure that subsequent major gatherings by the ministry were held at the stadium. Otti also offered to personally bear the cost of hiring the facility as his contribution to the ministry. “I have instructed the Honourable Commissioner for Youth and Sports Development that whenever you are having an event like this again, it should be held at the stadium. I know that using the stadium costs money, but I will pay. That will be my own contribution to the ministry,” he said. He added that the stadium could accommodate about 15,000 worshippers and promised to liaise with the General Overseer ahead of future programmes to ensure adequate arrangements. ‘I didn’t come here to campaign’ Otti explained that his presence at the crusade was not politically motivated but was to fulfil a promise he made to the General Overseer, Pastor Lazarus Muoka, during their recent meeting in Lagos. He, however, made a light-hearted political remark, saying there was no need to campaign at the gathering because the worshippers would naturally support him. “Why we can’t campaign here is that we already have all your votes,” the governor said. He thanked Muoka for his visit, prayers and spiritual support, assuring him of his administration’s continued partnership with the ministry. Otti also prayed for the growth of the church and God’s continued strengthening of its leadership and members. Earlier, Muoka had charged Christians to demonstrate genuine obedience to God by doing what He commands and refraining from whatever He forbids. He described obedience as fundamental to victorious Christian living, urging believers to guard their hearts, exercise self-discipline and resist temptations capable of compromising their faith. Muoka called on Christians to remain steadfast in God’s word and take divine instructions seriously. Top government officials accompanied the governor to the crusade. items.title: NADKANSCO to create 1,500 direct jobs and over 3,000 indirect jobs – MD
items.description: The Managing Director of NADKANSCO Cashew Processing Limited, Belinda Akorfa Adokpa, says the company is expected to create 1,500 direct jobs and more than 3,000 indirect jobs as it expands its cashew processing operations. She said the factory, which was established in 2012, struggled to operate consistently until the Ghana Export-Import Bank (Ghana EXIM Bank) intervened with financial support. Speaking at the commissioning of the facility by President John Dramani Mahama in Techiman on Monday, November 16, 2026, Mrs Adokpa said the bank’s intervention had provided a major boost to the company’s operations. She said the company would also train cashew farmers to improve production and ensure a consistent supply of raw materials to sustain the factory throughout the year. The training programme, she explained, forms part of efforts to strengthen the relationship between the company and farmers while addressing the challenge of seasonal supply shortages. “Your Excellency, this factory will create 1,500 direct jobs together with some 3,000 indirect jobs for farmers, transporters, aggregators and traders,” she said. “Majority of our workers are women,” she added. She said securing adequate quantities of raw cashew nuts was critical to keeping the factory operational throughout the year and sustaining the jobs expected to be created.

items.title: Lawyers submit affidavits detailing Nov 11 meeting with Imran, Bushra at Adiala jail
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Lawyers representing former prime minister Imran Khan and his wife, Bushra Bibi, have submitted affidavits to the Islamabad High Court (IHC), detailing their Nov 11 meeting with the incarcerated couple at Adiala jail. Meanwhile, Bushra has filed a fresh criminal miscellaneous application seeking the production of her complete medical record before the court and directions for her immediate transfer to a specialised hospital. The application, filed under Section 561-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure in Criminal Appeal No. 64 of 2025, seeks to place additional facts concerning Bushra’s deteriorating eyesight, alleged deficiencies in medical facilities and unhygienic conditions at Adiala jail on the judicial record. The application was diarised at the IHC on Nov 16, 2026, under diary number 22497/2026. It has been filed in connection with her pending appeal against her conviction in the £190 million Al-Qadir Trust case . Senior Advocate Sardar Muhammad Latif Khosa and Barrister Salman Safdar, who represent Imran and Bushra, submitted separate affidavits recounting their approximately three-hour meeting with the incarcerated couple on Nov 11. According to the affidavits, the meeting was arranged pursuant to an order passed by the IHC on November 10, directing the jail authorities to facilitate a meeting between Imran, Bushra and their lawyers at Adiala jail. The lawyers stated that they met the couple from 4pm to 7pm. During the first hour, Imran conveyed his instructions regarding the pending legal proceedings and his medical condition, while the subsequent discussion focused on Bushra’s deteriorating eyesight and the medical complications she was facing. The affidavits stated that Bushra informed the lawyers that she had been diagnosed with a mature cataract and that another surgery was scheduled to be performed on or around November 15, 2026. She also removed her dark grey sunglasses and showed the condition of her eyes to both lawyers, informing them that, according to the attending doctors, oil needed to be extracted from her eye. The lawyers stated in their affidavits that Bushra complained of severely impaired vision in both eyes following her previous surgical procedure . She also told them that she could see only to a limited extent while wearing spectacles and was virtually unable to see without them. Even with spectacles, she could perceive the lawyers sitting in front of her merely as indistinct dark objects, while her field of vision remained restricted to objects directly in front of her. She was unable to properly see objects on either side and had to estimate the position of objects and obstacles while moving around. The affidavits further stated that the former first lady had been experiencing persistent eye pain for several days and was taking two tablets each of Panadol and Tonoflex daily for pain relief. She also complained that despite repeatedly informing the jail authorities about the pain, specialist doctors attended to her only after a delay of approximately seven to eight days. According to the affidavits, the attending doctors had cautioned her that any infection following the impending eye surgery could result in complete and permanent loss of her eyesight. The lawyers also brought to the court’s notice the alleged unhygienic conditions of the room in which Bushra is confined at Adiala jail. According to the affidavits, she informed them that although she was accommodated in a large hall-type room, its sanitary conditions were seriously deficient. She alleged that rats and mice frequently entered the room, which was also infested with cockroaches, centipedes and other insects. As many as seven small snakes had reportedly been found inside the room and were subsequently killed and removed by a jail employee identified as Sibtain. The affected portions of the room were later cemented, according to the affidavits. The superintendent of the jail, however, refuted the reports of snakes in the room in a statement on Monday. Saying that the jail administration had taken notice of the reports in the media and circulating online, he added that the administration “strongly refutes” the claim, terming it “baseless, fabricated and contrary to the facts”. “All necessary actions are taken to provide health, protection, cleanliness and other conveniences to prisoners in Central Jail Adiala, including women prisoners, in accordance with the jail manual and rules and regulations,” the statement added, including the spraying of germicides and insecticides for an environment free of insects and harmful animals. Bushra also complained of frequent insect bites and resultant skin rashes, expressing apprehension that the unhygienic environment could expose her to an infection following eye surgery. The affidavits further stated that the duty medical officer at Adiala jail was a gynaecologist rather than an ophthalmologist, raising concerns about the availability of specialised eye care at the prison. Bushra further informed the lawyers that she had experienced bleeding following her previous surgery, which she attributed to unhygienic living conditions, inadequate medical supervision and a lack of specialised medical expertise. The fresh application states that Bushra had previously approached the IHC through a criminal miscellaneous application, seeking directions for the production of her complete medical record and provision of appropriate medical treatment. However, the applicant contends that an earlier meeting with her lawyer on Nov 2, 2026, lasted only around 40 minutes after a gap of approximately 11 months, leaving her unable to explain the full extent of her medical complications. The application also refers to a report submitted by the Islamabad advocate general to the Supreme Court on Aug 17, 2026, regarding the medical treatment provided to Imran and Bushra. According to the application, medical records furnished by the Adiala jail superintendent had revealed that Bushra’s eye condition required urgent medical intervention. Consequently, she had twice been taken outside the prison for surgery and medical examination. The application further claimed that during the Nov 2 meeting, Bushra complained that she was unable to tolerate sunlight or artificial light and had difficulty opening her eyes and seeing clearly. She also expressed dissatisfaction with the medical treatment being provided at the jail and said she wanted to be examined and treated by doctors of her own choice. The application alleges that despite medical advice recommending major surgery, the jail authorities had not provided Bushra, her family or her legal team with the relevant medical notes, diagnostic reports or prescriptions. Instead, they had verbally informed them about the need for another major surgical procedure around Nov 15 and the risk of permanent loss of eyesight if it was not performed. In her latest criminal miscellaneous application, Bushra has requested the court to take on record the additional facts and circumstances disclosed during the Nov 11 meeting and consider them alongside the grounds raised in her earlier application. She has specifically sought directions for the respondents, including the state, Adiala jail superintendent, deputy superintendent and NAB chairman, to produce her complete medical record before the court. The applicant has also requested the court to ensure the timely provision of all necessary medical and surgical treatment and direct her immediate transfer to a specialised hospital for appropriate medical care. The application maintains that the additional facts concerning her deteriorating eyesight, impending surgery and conditions inside the jail warrant urgent judicial intervention to protect her health and prevent irreversible loss of vision.
